VAGINAL BLEEDING IN THE ED 
 
 
IMMEDIATE ED INVESTIGATIONS 
 
* VBG and urine pregnancy test 
* Bedside ultrasound 
 
- viable intrauterine pregnancy (threatened) 
 
- non-viable intrauterine pregnancy (missed / incomplete) 
 
- empty uterus (complete / ectopic) 
 
- free fluid & empty uterus (ruptured ectopic) 
SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT 
ECTOPIC PREGANCY 
 
*Resuscitate as for haemorrhagic shock  
 
*Urgent gynae referral 
INCOMPLETE MISCARRIAGE 
 
*Rub up uterus  
*Expel products as much as possible  
*Start Oxytocin 20 units in 1 L fluid at 125ml/hr, NB! may worsen hypotension 
SEPTIC INCOMPLETE MISCARRIAGE 
 
*Fluid bolus 20ml/kg 
 
*Bloods – blood gas, U&E, FBC, INR, crossmatch (if indicated), ± DIC screen 
 
*IV Antibiotics – AugmentinÒ 30mg/kg 
 
*Refer to sepsis & septic shock protocol 
PLACENTA PRAEVIA:  
*NO DIGITAL PV EXAM if suspected àconfirmed on US  
 
*Urgent obstetric referral 
SUSPECTED ABRUPTIO PLACENTAE/UTERINE RUPTURE 
 
*Urgent obstetric consult for theatre, resus as per ABCs 
POSTPARTUM HAEMORRHAGE 
 
*Rub up uterus, expel products 
*Oxytocin 20 units in 1 L fluid at 125ml/hr, NB! may worsen hypotension 
*Tranexamic acid 1g IV over 10mins 
 
*Empty bladder, insert catheter 
*Exclude cervical/vaginal trauma 
*Urgent theatre if suspected uterine rupture/inversion 
*Consider balloon tamponade of uterus if bleeding persists 
PREGNANCY RELATED CAUSES 
 
* Ectopic pregnancy 
* Miscarriage 
  
- threatened (os closed) 
 
- incomplete (os open, products) 
 
- complete (no products) 
 
- missed 
* Antepartum haemorrhage (>24 weeks)  
 
- placenta praevia 
 
- abruptio placenta 
 
- uterine rupture 
* Secondary postpartum haemorrhage 
UNSTABLE 
RAPID TRIAGE TO RESUS 
 
* ABCs  
 
* Insert 2 x IV lines; Blood gas; U&E; FBC; Crossmatch 
 
* Consider fluid bolus (10ml/kg) 
 
* Emergency blood – CHECK Rh OR GIVE Rh NEGATIVE BLOOD! 
* Consider need for anti-D in Rh negative pts (can be given in ward   within 72 hrs) 
 
* Crossmatch emergency blood & blood products based on   
                    patient’s haemodynamic status 
 
* Contact gynae on call urgently, consider informing theatre 
* If still bleeding consider Tranexamic acid 1g IV 
STABLE 
 CLOSE MONITORING IN 165 – MAY BECOME UNSTABLE 
* GYNAE/GOPD referral for w/u if gynae pathology suspected 
* MOPD if general cause suspected 
* Ferrous sulphate 200mg bd po for anaemia 
* Tranexamic acid 500mg – 1g tds po for 3/7 
* Consider oral contraceptive in abnormal uterine bleeding 
NON-PREGNANCY RELATED CAUSES 
 
*Gynaecological 
 
- Benign – fibroid uterus, polyp 
 
- Malignancy – uterus / cervix 
 
- Infection 
 
- Trauma 
 
- Endometriosis & adenomyosis 
 
- DUB 
*General 
 
- Clotting disorders 
 
- Hypothyroidism 
 
- Hepatic/renal disease 
HISTORY 
* Bleeding – duration, amount, presence of  
   clots, associated symptoms (LAP, PV discharge, fever) 
* LNMP, Contraception use and type 
* Medical, obstetric and gynae history including medications 
Dr J du Plessis / Dr R Gihwala CMJAH E
